findings.title: In-place downsize can corrupt the upload and strips animation
findings.body: Auto-downsize calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the same path for source and destination (the open upload Tempfile). ImageMagick convert and gifsicle are not safe that way: the output open truncates the file before it is fully read, and many versions write a temp file then rename it over the destination. The Tempfile fd stays on the old inode, while tempfile.size (fstat on that fd) is what both the while condition and Upload.create_for use as the filesize. After a replace, the recorded size can be the original multi-megabyte size while the path holds the smaller image, or create_for can persist the pre-downsize bytes / a truncated file. The return value is ignored, so a failed convert is retried and the damaged file is still passed to create_for. The loop can also exit while the file is still over max_image_size_kb (five 80% passes are not guaranteed to hit the byte limit, and a no-op or failed pass does not abort), despite the comment claiming the image is reduced to the allowed size. Rack multipart tempfiles are created as Tempfile.new("RackMultipart") and have no suffix, but optimize only selects the animated pipeline when the source path matches /\.GIF$/i, and the still instructions always run convert ...[0]. A large GIF is therefore flattened to the first frame even when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, and ImageMagick keys the writer off the destination suffix, so an extension-less output can fail or be written in the wrong format while original_filename and content_type stay unchanged. If the path does end in .gif, downsize_instructions_animated forwards the "80%" geometry to gifsicle --resize-fit, which was built for a pixel WIDTHxHEIGHT box, so animated downsize fails instead of shrinking the file.

findings.title: Second downsize definition replaces the width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods. The new downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 completely replaces downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145, so the width/height wrapper is dead and never runs. The previous public signature passed numeric width and height (and an optional opts hash) into optimize, which formatted "WxH". Existing callers that still use that shape now bind height to opts; optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError because an Integer has no []. Callers that also pass an options hash raise ArgumentError (5 arguments for arity 3..4). optimize itself changed from (operation, from, to, width, height, opts) to (operation, from, to, dimensions, opts), and OptimizedImage.dimensions was removed, so any external caller of those methods with separate width and height breaks the same way. The upload controller only works because it uses the string form that accidentally overwrote the compatibility wrapper.

findings.title: Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type
findings.body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments each honored the admin setting. It now rejects every file larger than a hardcoded 10240 KB. Attachments are not downsized by this feature, so a site with max_attachment_size_kb under 10240 no longer gets a client-side rejection (the file is uploaded and fails later), and a site that allows attachments over 10 MB can no longer select them in the composer. Images are also blocked at 10 MB even when max_image_size_kb is higher, so previously valid images never reach the server. The 413 handler at line 246 uses the same literal, so the alert always says the maximum is 10240 KB, which is wrong when the configured limit or the proxy body limit is different. This number is a separate copy from the controller's 10.megabytes cap, so the client and server ceilings can drift.

findings.title: Multipart images are converted with no size ceiling
findings.body: The new loop runs OptimizedImage.downsize up to five times whenever an image is larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Nothing in that condition caps how large the file may be. The 10 MB ceiling added in this change is only applied to API URL fetches (FileHelper.download) and the browser check; a normal multipart POST never goes through that helper, and the client check is bypassable. create only requires a logged-in user, and the convert runs inside the deferred upload job before Upload.create_for can reject the file. Any member can therefore force repeated ImageMagick decodes of whatever body the web server accepts, including decompression bombs whose pixel buffer is far larger than the file size. A failing downsize does not break the loop, so one bad file always costs five process spawns.

findings.title: URL upload fetch limit no longer follows the site setting
findings.body: API URL uploads used to be fetched up to SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. They are now stopped at a hardcoded 10.megabytes, for every type, not only images that will be downsized. On a site whose max_image_size_kb is above 10240, URL uploads the setting still allows (this fetch cap has always applied to non-images as well) are no longer downloaded, so the new downsize path never sees them. The ceiling is not configurable and is a different literal from the client-side 10 * 1024 check, so the two limits can diverge.

findings.title: No coverage for downsize or the new upload ceiling
findings.body: This change adds an upload-time convert loop, a new OptimizedImage.downsize calling convention, and replaces site-setting size checks with a hardcoded 10 MB cap in the client, the 413 message, and FileHelper.download. No tests were added for success or failure of that loop, in-place Tempfile conversion, GIF/animation handling, files that stay over max_image_size_kb after five attempts, or attachments versus images under a non-default max_*_size_kb. Those paths can store a truncated image or ignore the configured limits, and nothing in the PR would fail if they did.
